(CIK 1666700, accession 0001666700-26-000013, filed February 17, 2026) and its 2026 proxy statement (DEF 14A, accession 0001193125-26-151204, ownership as of April 7, 2026). Ellen Kullman is a former CEO of the predecessor E. I. du Pont de Nemours and Company (EIDP). She does not appear anywhere in the 2026 proxy, whose table covers current directors and nominees, current named executive officers and more-than-5% holders, so status is no-reported-stake. COMPANY CHANGES: on November 1, 2025 DuPont completed the spin-off of its electronics business as Qnity Electronics, Inc.; the Electronics, Aramids (sold April 1, 2026) and earlier M&M businesses are reported as discontinued operations, so the FY2025 10-K recasts net sales to $6,849 million (continuing operations) and figures here are not comparable with the FY2024 edition ($12,386 million). DuPont also effected a 1-for-3 reverse stock split on June 24, 2026 (Q3 2026 10-Q); the proxy share counts are before it, and percentages are unaffected. 5% HOLDERS: both rest on Schedule 13G amendments reporting holdings at the end of 2023, so they are stale relative to the April 2026 share count. DIVIDENDS: $597 million paid to stockholders; distributions to noncontrolling interests ($9 million) are a separate line and excluded. BUYBACKS: the cash-flow line 'Purchases of common stock and forward contracts' ($500m) is cash paid to repurchase DuPont's own stock (tagged with a company-specific XBRL concept, so no xbrl object); the $8 million excise tax paid on treasury stock purchases is a separate line and not included. STOCK COMP: the continuing-operations cash-flow add-back ($38 million; the FY2025 10-K recast 2024 to $56 million). GEOGRAPHY: continuing operations; China/Hong Kong was $708 million within Asia Pacific. No broad employee stock purchase plan was identified in the 10-K, so plan is null.
